findings.problem: SensorWorkflow uses pub fields with primitive types (String, bool) allowing every combination of status, is_validated, is_sent, including illegal states such as status='sent' with is_sent=false, or is_sent=true with is_validated=false.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid lifecycle state can be constructed and mutated freely; no runtime or compile-time enforcement of valid state transitions.
findings.fix: Replace status: String + lifecycle bools with a typed enum/state-machine typestate (e.g. enum SensorStatus { New, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }). Make fields private with a fallible constructor.

findings.problem: No enum or typestate for SensorWorkflow lifecycle. Status is a free-form String and lifecycle is encoded as separate bools (is_validated, is_sent).
findings.failure_mode: The compiler cannot enforce valid transitions; callers can set status to arbitrary strings, or set is_sent without is_validated. Invalid state combinations are representable and silently accepted.
findings.fix: Define `enum SensorStatus { New, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }`. Replace `status: String`, `is_validated: bool`, `is_sent: bool`, and `sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64>` with a single `status: SensorStatus` field.

findings.problem: id is pub String with no domain newtype. Any string is accepted as a valid sensor ID with no length, format, or uniqueness enforcement.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid IDs (empty, malformed, too long) propagate into the domain core without rejection at the parse boundary.
findings.fix: Define `pub struct SensorId(String)` or `pub struct SensorId([u8; N])` with a fallible constructor that enforces domain rules. Replace `id: String` with `id: SensorId`.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes a mutable SensorWorkflow by value and mutates fields in-place (item.status = "sent".to_string(); item.is_sent = true;). This is imperative mutation in the core rather than a pure function producing a new valid state.
findings.failure_mode: The core function does not enforce preconditions (e.g., must be validated before sent) and can produce invalid states. Mutation in-place bypasses typestate invariants.
findings.fix: Make mark_sent a pure function: `fn mark_sent(workflow: &SensorWorkflow) -> Result<SensorWorkflow, WorkflowError>` that constructs a new SensorWorkflow with SensorStatus::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: now() } after validating the source state is Validated.

findings.problem: item.status = "sent".to_string() allocates a new String for every call and stores an unbounded status string in the struct. This violates bounded allocation discipline and functional core principles.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation per call, and the status string accepts arbitrary values (not just domain-valid transitions).
findings.fix: Replace String status with a zero-sized enum variant. When using SensorStatus::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms }, no status String allocation is needed.

findings.problem: mark_sent has no error return type. It cannot signal failure states such as invalid preconditions, invalid state transitions, or allocation errors.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid transitions are silently accepted or silently ignored instead of being returned as typed errors per the domain error taxonomy.
findings.fix: Add `Result<SensorWorkflow, WorkflowError>` return type with a typed error enum covering InvalidTransition, InvalidState, and Allocation.

findings.problem: Unnecessary heap allocation via .to_string() on a literal in the inner loop. No allocation awareness, no try_reserve, no borrowed/Cow alternatives.
findings.failure_mode: Every call to mark_sent allocates a new String on the heap, causing allocation churn under load with no measurable performance benefit over an enum.
findings.fix: Replace String status with enum SensorStatus. The enum variant carries no heap data, eliminating the allocation entirely.

findings.problem: The entire crate is data + mutation with no functional core / imperative shell separation. mark_sent is an impure mutation function that performs side effects (string allocation) instead of a pure calculation.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot unit-test the pure logic independently of I/O; the struct and mutation are exposed directly, making the boundary between data and actions undefined.
findings.fix: Define pure data types (SensorStatus enum, SensorId newtype) and a pure transition function mark_sent. Move any I/O, clock access (for sent_at_epoch_ms), logging, and persistence into a shell module.

findings.problem: All fields are pub with no fallible constructor or smart constructor. External code can construct SensorWorkflow with any combination of invalid fields directly.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid state can be created at any boundary, not just the parse boundary. The invariant 'validated must be true before sent' is unenforceable.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Add `impl SensorWorkflow { pub fn new(id: SensorId) -> Self { ... } }` and state-transition methods that are the sole constructors for derived states.

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for mark_sent or any performance claim about the crate. The .to_string() allocation pattern has no measured cost or baseline.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify that allocation-free enum replacement improves or maintains performance in the target workload.
findings.fix: Add a criterion or divan benchmark comparing the current String-based mark_sent vs the enum-based mark_sent, with workload, baseline, command, and variance.

findings.problem: No profiler data (flamegraph, perf, samply) exists to validate the allocation profile or identify hot paths.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot confirm that the String allocation in mark_sent is a hotspot or that enum replacement would materially help.
findings.fix: Run `cargo flamegraph` or `samply record` on a representative workload and report the allocation profile.

findings.problem: No second-ring evidence (cargo clippy, cargo test, cargo miri, cargo kani) reported or present.
findings.failure_mode: Static review cannot catch all classes of bugs; no command evidence to corroborate the review.
findings.fix: Run `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, and `cargo miri test` on the refactored crate. Report command outcomes.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or any performance claim
no profiler data (flamegraph/samply/perf) for allocation analysis
no second-ring command evidence (cargo test, cargo clippy, cargo miri, cargo kani)
no allocation audit (no try_reserve, no checked arithmetic, no capacity planning anywhere)
residual_risk: Static review only; no commands run. The crate is structurally non-compliant with Holzman Rust: no typestate, no domain newtypes, no error taxonomy, no functional core / imperative shell split, and unnecessary heap allocations in the core. All findings are remediable by replacing primitive fields with typed enums/newtypes and refactoring mark_sent into a pure transition function with Result error returns.
